newsitem.title: USA: Twins found emaciated, encrusted with excrement.
newsitem.headline: Twins found emaciated, encrusted with excrement.

text.p: Five-year-old twin girls were discovered emaciated, crawling with ants and encrusted with excrement and their mother was charged with attempted murder and torture on Tuesday, police said.

The girls, who suffer from cerebral palsy, were severely malnourished, dehydrated and bruised when they were found in bunkbeds in a house in Ceres, 80 miles (130 kms) east of San Francisco, on Sunday night, police said.
"You could picture the worst Holocaust victim you've seen -- starving victims in concentration camps -- it was very similar to that," Ceres Police Sgt. Allen McKay said.
"It was horrifying, shocking. It was beyond anything I'd imagined," he said, adding that the twins weighed just 14 and 19 pounds and "were just basically skin and bones."
Their mother, 26-year-old Tanya Walker, was arrested on Sunday night and jailed.
A police statement said the girls were "suffering from scabies, had dried stool particles around their buttocks and had ants crawling in and out of bodily orifices."
They were in critical in Oakland Children's Hospital on Tuesday, police said.

Walker was initially charged with felony child endangerment. On Tuesday, she was also charged with two counts of attempted murder and two counts of torture, charges that can carry a life prison sentence, police said.

The girls' grandparents found them alone, locked inside Walker's home on Sunday when they were returning two siblings from a weekend visit. The grandparents took the twins to a nearby hospital and police were notified. The twins were later flown to Oakland.

At the time the children were found, Walker had gone to pick up her infant son from a babysitter. Walker also has two other healthy children, the 3-year-old son and 7-year-old daughter who had been visiting the grandparents. The three other children were released to relatives, police said.

Walker told police that government funding was cut off for a nutritional formula that had been prescribed for the twins. She tried other foods but the twins lost weight and their condition deteriorated to a point where she was afraid to seek medical help because she was concerned authorities would take her other children away from her, McKay said.
